title: Space A Hub — C1: MCP Tool Contract
description: Tools exposed by the Space A MCP server to employee agents (Pillar 1 and any MCP client). Change policy: additive only. Adding optional fields or enum values is allowed; removing/renaming fields or changing their meaning is not. Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields.

transport.description: Every C1 call carries identity and trace metadata OUT OF BAND — in transport headers, not in tool arguments. MCP's own auth spec is not mature, so this is defined at the application layer. Identity is the precondition for the visibility model: without it, 'team' filtering cannot be computed at all.

Authorization.description: Issued by corporate SSO. The server resolves it to { user_id, agent_id, team, scopes }. NOTE: team and agent_id are derived from this token and are NOT accepted as request parameters — letting a client assert its own team would void the whole permission model.

X-Space-A-Trace-Id.description: Correlates one problem-solving flow across agents. The originating caller generates it. If absent, the server issues one and returns it.

X-Space-A-Depth.description: How many agent hops deep this call is. Increment when acting on a Space A response by calling another agent. Server rejects depth > MAX_DEPTH (default 5) with rate_limited. This is a cooperative guard against runaway loops, not a defence against a malicious client; the hard backstop is the server-side token/call circuit breaker.

stdio.SPACE_A_TOKEN: Same token, passed as an environment variable at process launch (local development).

visibility.description: Knowledge sharing scope. Omitting this yields 'team' — the safe default, so an agent that makes no judgment call cannot leak a secret org-wide. Agents may narrow to 'private' freely; widening to 'public' must be explicit.

context.description: Anchors for graph expansion. The richer this is, the fewer tokens the answer needs.

tools.description: MCP tools / CLIs in play, e.g. ['pnpm', 'docker']

code.description: unauthorized = missing/expired token. forbidden = authenticated but out of scope. rate_limited = depth exceeded or circuit breaker tripped.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the org's agent knowledge for a similar past issue and its solution. Call this BEFORE trying to reason a fix from scratch. Returns a condensed solution payload, not raw logs.

query.description: The error message or problem statement. Raw text is fine.

limit.description: Keep small. Every extra result is tokens spent.

tried_and_failed.description: Dead ends a previous agent already walked. Do not repeat them.

related.description: Graph-expanded neighbours. This is what a vector-only search cannot give you.

reuse_count.description: How many times this solution has been reused successfully. Higher = more trustworthy.

searched.description: Retrieval funnel. Proves the token saving: many candidates considered, few returned.

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Record an issue and its solution AFTER you have solved it. Single call — there is deliberately no separate 'open' step, because an agent that dies before resolving would leave an orphan record, and an unresolved record is not knowledge.

tried_steps.description: What you tried that did NOT work. As valuable as the solution — it saves the next agent the same dead ends.

source_issue_id.description: If you solved this by reusing an existing entry, cite it. This is what makes reuse_count and the knowledge-flow graph possible.

status.description: 'merged' means the gatekeeper judged this a duplicate and folded it into an existing entry — the first line of defence against knowledge-base bloat.

tools.name: get_skill_candidates
tools.description: List repeated solution patterns that should be promoted into an automated Skill. A fix recorded 3+ times is a signal that a human should stop doing it by hand.
